title: A festival street through the rooftops
body: You remembered people moving here. There never was such a version: the only take ever made told the figures to stay put. Now the Moon is whole, lower and amber, sky lanterns rise over the lake, and a crowd walks a lantern-lit street. The street is new to the picture. It is there because figures shut inside walled courtyards could only shuffle on the spot.
opts: Unbroken rooftops, with people who only turn and gesture
That version exists and can be wired in.

title: The card, and the Chinese name
body: English as you wrote it. The Chinese is mine and needs your eye: 这一次，全世界的航天计划共建国际月球基地, in five columns with the name largest. 国际月球基地 is also the name at 1:45 and in the subtitles.
q: Is this the Chinese you want?
opts: Write the wording in the note.

title: The walkout, and what the cases are
body: The cases are portable ventilators. A sealed launch suit has no air of its own until it is plugged into the spacecraft, so Apollo and Soyuz crews carry a small fan unit to the pad, with its hose plugged in at the belly. Crew Dragon, Artemis and recent Shenzhou crews carry nothing. In eight reference photographs nobody walks in step. The four now come toward us across a wet apron with the lit rocket behind, each at their own rhythm; the units are lunch-box size with the hose plugged in at both ends, and the rocket is the same one as at 0:19 and 1:17. What falls short: this painting is more softly modelled than the flat crew picture that follows it.
q: Tick what you want changed (leave unticked to keep).
opts: Flatten this painting to match the shot after it

title: The eclipse over Anatolia
body: The toy globe now has real coastlines, checked against a map, and the Moon's shadow sits on central Anatolia in all three views of the lesson. T's cheeks are fuller here and everywhere else he appears; his character sheet was the thing that was wrong. The shadow is a dark core about the size of Anatolia with a soft edge. A crisp disc would be truer to a small lamp, and would cover everything from Greece to the Caspian. Separately, the toy Earth on your desk at 0:58, floating at 1:33 and on the parapet at 3:19 still has invented continents.
q: Tick what you want changed (leave unticked to keep).
opts: Make the shadow crisper or smaller
Paint the same real map on the toy Earth at 0:58, 1:33 and 3:19

title: The envelope, handed over and opened
body: Three shots at real speed. Kenton's hand gives you the envelope and leaves, and the front stays readable. You turn it over with both hands and the flap falls open. A letter folded in three comes out and its top opens to show lines of print. What falls short: the cut at 0:59 jumps a little within the turn, and the envelope is about one and a half times true size against your hands, which keeps the words readable. There is no seal on the flap now.
q: Tick what you want changed (leave unticked to keep).
opts: The words on it get smaller.
Seal the flap with a small pale-blue-dot sticker

title: The sung close-up, with a still upper face
body: The sung close-up is in the film. Everything except your mouth is now the painted portrait, stable, which fixes the glitching upper face. The cost: your jaw and chin do not move, only the lips and the inside of the mouth. The take's lower face would not fit the portrait, so the two could not be joined along the cheeks. In frames it reads as a moving mouth on a still face. Please judge it at speed.
opts: Go back to the non-singing shot
Paint a new portrait with the chin clear of the neck ring, so the jaw can drop
A new painting over your photo, then a new take.

title: One station design
more: 0:25: the tower at its true height
body: The plan is redrawn in the same ink style from the 3D model, so it is the station seen everywhere else. The old one had the comms tower in the wrong place and twice too large, masts two to three times too tall, and no cable or rovers. The roundel replaces the red seal and is a fifth smaller than my first try. Two other pictures were brought to the model: the tower at 0:25 and the lit windows at 2:23. What differs now is the hand: the mounds are soft hatched heaps on this plan and peaked heaps at 0:25 and 2:23, where the old plan had painted rocks.
q: Tick what you want changed (leave unticked to keep).
opts: Repaint the plan's mounds with the old brushwork, on the same footprints
Draw the mounds the same way in all three shots
Say which look in the note.

title: The glove is the right size
body: Your question, with numbers: against the 3 cm cups the glove's forefinger is about 13 mm thick. That is a bare hand in a thin glove, and about half the bulk of a real heavy lab gauntlet. It reads as large because the cups are the size of bottle caps and the hand is nearest the lens. Nothing was rescaled. She now leans in as the glove slides the card to the plant, so the body and the hand move in one beat, and the breath fog is gone.
opts: Make it a bulkier, truer gauntlet
About twice the size in frame; it would crowd the plant.

title: Seventeen lights, the ones the station has
body: The mounds no longer have windows, since they are under metres of soil. The lights that come on are the ones the model has from this camera: the dome first, then the tower's windows, the portholes of two tunnels and the airlock node. The counter reads 17 / 17. It is quieter than with 26.
opts: Add work lamps on the masts and along the road
The station model would get them too.

title: Single mode on the TV
body: The TV shows single mode: four targets, with the arrows it scores matching the panels Kenton and T step on, still on the film's beats. I had no picture of your game in single mode, so the four targets sit in the left half, the game's default for a single first player. T's cheek is fuller here too.
q: Where do the targets sit on your setup?

title: The odd hand was a third hand
body: Lúcia's right hand was already on her chest; the hand hovering over the tablet was a third one, child-sized. It is gone. She keeps her hand on her heart and tips her head to Kenji's shoulder, which means she no longer waves at the dog on the screen. Kenji's glasses go white with the tablet's reflection in some frames.
opts: Paint a proper wave back in

title: One fingertip to her hand
body: One index finger goes out to M's raised hand on the screen and rests there, at 2:44 and again at 2:49. The shoulder, elbow and forearm were posed with a 3D figure at your height, and the screen now stands a real arm's reach away. Your profile is the original painting, untouched. In the split screen your profile is cut just behind the glasses so that M's hand stays in the picture. The fingertip stops a few pixels short of her fingers, with a point of light between.
q: How should the split screen frame you?
opts: Make the split uneven so my whole profile shows
Show my whole profile and lose more of the screen

title: The toast, restaged as one moment
more: The wide: one arm each, forward and up
body: All three shots now share one staging. In the wide everyone faces the glass and raises one arm forward and up with a straight wrist, as in your reference; nobody sips, so the continuity slip is gone, and the ground outside matches the station model. The realistic Adaeze close-up is replaced by a flat profile: her arm one line to her cup, a tear, her eyes on the Earth. From any camera in front of her, an arm raised toward the Earth foreshortened into a cup thrust at the lens. In the two-cup shot each hand continues its forearm. What falls short: the wide is a wholly new painting, a shade more violet-grey, and its figures wear dark shoes; Adaeze's shot has little motion beyond breath and the tear.
q: Tick what you want changed (leave unticked to keep).
opts: Put Chen Yu beside Adaeze in her shot
He stands next to her in the wide.
Socks, not shoes, in the wide

title: The reunion, with Kenton coming in
more: The tear closes below the faces
The close painting of the hug
body: Kenton now walks in from the doorway, crouches and kneels at the near edge of the hug with his back to us, one hand on T's back. The rejoining tear sits lower and crosses floor, legs and your back, never a face. The close view is its own painting with its own small movement, not an enlargement. What falls short: while Kenton walks he is seen from the shoulders down; for the first second he stands small in the doorway facing us, as before; one stretch of his walk plays at double speed and has not been judged in motion; and he and T look shod indoors.
q: Tick what you want changed (leave unticked to keep).
opts: A wider picture so Kenton is whole while he walks
Kenton from behind in the opening second too
Use the take where he wraps both arms round all three

title: Lyrics and the camera, whole film
body: The jerk at 0:33 was the engine's own pan: it sat still for most of a second and then jumped to speed. It is now one slow move. Sung lines no longer wipe on. English words fade in whole; short or fast lines fade in once or are simply there at the cut; each Chinese character is brushed on its own note. The specks at 0:47 were the next word's ink leaking through the old wipe. A separate fault that made eight shots step unevenly is fixed in the engine. Two small calls remain.
q: Tick what you want changed (leave unticked to keep).
opts: 0:33: cut into a pan that is already drifting, not one that starts from rest
0:57 and 1:22: brush each character on its own note, even if one is half-written at the cut
Now 三人 and 思念 arrive as pairs, the second character half a second early.

title: International Moonbase
body: Every caption, card, label and subtitle says International Moonbase / 国际月球基地. The red seal is gone. No painted picture carried the old name; the one place it was baked in, a byline on the laptop at 1:05, is corrected. Folder and file names inside the project keep the old word so nothing breaks.

title: The terrace over the Huangpu
body: You settle from a crouch onto one knee, breathe, and turn a little toward M, whose raised arms wobble. The river carries what photographs of that reach show: a tarpaulined cargo barge and a coal barge, the white cross-river ferry, a three-deck sightseeing boat outlined in coloured light, and a light-strung mock sailing ship. None of the reference photographs shows a barge at night, so the barges' lights are a guess.

title: The reading finger
body: The finger runs down the column in one glide. It never went back up; the old timing made it stop and start five times. The line is sung just after this shot, so the finger reads ahead of your voice.

title: The headphones
body: Your face was held from the painting while the headphones were redrawn from the take, so they slid up to 18 pixels against your head. They now ride with the head.

title: The chin
body: From 1:09.3 the take's own jaw came out from under the painted face as a second chin line. It is gone. Your head now moves about half as far in this shot.

title: The whole plume
body: Three flickering flames, a column of smoke that lengthens and thins as the rocket climbs, and a ground cloud that keeps rolling for the whole shot.

title: M's hair on launch day
body: The two paintings already agreed; the takes had changed her hair, to three braids at 0:27 and no braid at 1:19. Both now carry the painted hair: one side braid, a pink elastic, a curly tail. It reads slightly redder at 1:19 in the flame's light.

title: T's cheeks
body: T's character sheet was corrected, since you said it three times, and his face was repainted to it here, in the lesson, the viewing room at 1:29, the playroom, the call home at 2:38 and the reunion.

title: The left elbow
body: The painted elbow stayed behind as a stub while the redrawn arm drifted up. Fixed, along with a smaller copy of the same fault under the raised arm.

title: Astronaut legs
body: At 1:41 the take shuffled on the spot and was played at a speed that made the drawing stutter about three times a second; it is a new take with long planted strides. At 1:50 smeared shins were being blended onto painted boots; the whole figure is now drawn from the same movement. The 1:50 figure sways in small uneven steps, not perfectly fluidly. Every other suited shot was checked frame by frame and no leg fault was found.

title: The rooftop
body: T's arm is already moving at the cut and does not stop: the beam climbs the tree, sweeps the sky and finds the toy Moon as 月 is sung. The lit Moon is the brightest thing in the frame, and Kenton has his back to us. What falls short: for about half a second the beam points up while the drawn flashlight lies level in his fist, and the last half second is close to still.

title: Your face is out of this passage
body: It goes from Adaeze to Layla to 乡. Both small sky labels are gone.

title: The valve and the needle
body: One slow continuous turn, anticlockwise to open. The needle is drawn by the engine: it trembles from the first frame, starts to rise a third of a second after the valve opens, and lags the wheel.

title: Chen Yu's vermilion
body: True vermilion is back on his collar here and on his name card at 1:48. Blotchy marks on the back of his neck at 2:34, left by the earlier colour change, are gone.
